summary: An external retrieval located primary statute text and congressional records for 21 records whose earlier research rested on secondary reports or on searches that this environment cannot run. Research subagents opened the U.S. Code pages reproduced by Cornell's Legal Information Institute (counted as primary text when their amendment notes cite the enacting Public Law section and date), Congressional Research Service reports, enrolled public laws on govinfo and bill status files from the Library of Congress; five independent reviewers re-opened the deciding copies and rewrote the records. No stage changed. Corrections: the 2025 tax law's estate exclusion of 15 million dollars applies from 2026 with inflation indexing for decedents dying after 2026, and its state and local tax cap is 40,000 dollars for 2025, 40,400 for 2026 and 101 percent of the prior year through 2029 before reverting to 10,000 (c22-02); the advanced manufacturing credit ends for wind components after 2027 and phases out for critical minerals after 2033 (c22-02); the FY2026 energy and water act's section 311 transfers of unobligated balances total 5.165 billion dollars per CRS (c12-03); the AGOA extension allows refunds on request for entries after its lapse rather than automatic retroactivity (c09-06). Bills found by congressional searches were confirmed from their status files and recorded as related context where they differ from the recommendation (c12-11, c26-17, c24-07, c18-35, c22-19, c05-33); the enacted FY2026 bar on transferring ATF functions is recorded as a blocker on c22-25. Confidence rose on 11 records and fell on none. Counts unchanged: 115 in effect of 627 counted.
title: Statute and congressional-record pass over 21 records
